plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: Towering stalks carry huge golden faces that follow the sun across the sky. In early September, fields of them glow like pools of sunshine, with seed-heavy brown centers surrounded by bright yellow rays.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early autumn (July to September) in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Great Plains of North America and farm fields across Europe
plants.funFact: A sunflower head is not a single flower. It is made up of hundreds or even thousands of tiny florets, and each one can become a seed.

plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: Pale lilac-pink goblets rise straight from bare ground in damp meadows. Their leaves appeared months earlier and have already died back, so the flowers seem to appear from nowhere as summer fades.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to autumn (August to October)
plants.location: Damp meadows and woodland edges across western and central Europe
plants.funFact: Despite its name, it isn't a true crocus. It is a member of the lily family and contains colchicine, a toxic compound that is also used in medicine and in plant breeding.

plants.name: Acacia pycnantha
plants.description: Branches become covered in fluffy, fragrant golden pom-poms. Flowering begins in the last weeks of the Southern Hemisphere winter, and the blooms announce spring across southeastern Australia.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring (August to October) in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Southeastern Australia, including Victoria, South Australia and New South Wales
plants.funFact: Golden Wattle is Australia's national floral emblem. National Wattle Day is celebrated on September 1, the first day of spring.
